page: Microsoft Azure DC32ds_v3 is a dedicated x86_64 server instance belonging to the DDCSv3 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, translating to 8 GB of RAM per core, and includes 2458 GB of local storage. The virtualization layer is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 17264.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 49816.66, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. The processor's cryptographic capabilities are highlighted by a strong Passmark CPU encryption test score of 36927.97, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets. Memory performance shows a read-only large block bandwidth of 170.27 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 69.27 GB/sec.

This instance is highly suited for database operations and static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 48.38 GB/sec. It also demonstrates strong efficiency in prompt processing for small language models, reaching 2469.96 tokens/sec. However, without a dedicated GPU, it exhibits a clear tradeoff in large-scale AI workloads, as text generation for a 70B parameter model drops to a weak 2.64 tokens/sec. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high-density memory and storage configuration, making it a resource-efficient choice for enterprise databases, memory-intensive applications, and secure cryptographic workloads.

It is equipped with 256 GB of RAM (8 GB per core) and 2458 GB of local storage, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 17264.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 49816.66.
